record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: Given an infinite discrete collection of positive point masses a_k located at x_k in R^n, assume the gravitational force field F(x) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ a_k (x_k - x) / |x - x_k|^n converges under the summability condition Σ a_k / |x_k|^{n-1} < ∞. Must this force field always vanish at some point; equivalently, must the associated logarithmic or Newtonian potential always have a critical point?

evidence.quote: Question: For an infinite discrete set of point masses in space, is it always true that the force created by these masses vanishes at some point?
The question is whether every such F has at least one zero.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\{x_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an infinite discrete set of points (with no finite accumulation point), and let $\{a_k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers ("masses") satisfying the convergence condition
$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{a_k}{|x_k|^{n-1}} < \infty.$$
Define the associated gravitational force field on $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{x_k : k \geq 0\}$ by
$$F(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k \, \frac{x_k - x}{|x - x_k|^n}.$$
Equivalently, $F = -\nabla U$, where $U$ is the corresponding logarithmic ($n=2$) or Newtonian ($n \geq 3$) potential generated by the masses $a_k$ at the points $x_k$.

Question: Must there always exist a point $x^* \in \mathbb{R}^n \setminus \{x_k\}$ with $F(x^*) = 0$? Equivalently, must $U$ always possess at least one critical point?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the Clunie–Eremenko–Rossi conjecture, posed in their 1993 paper "On equilibrium points of logarithmic and Newtonian potentials" (J. London Math. Soc.). Subsequent work by Eremenko, Langley, Rossi and others has obtained partial results and an "operator version," but the original conjecture concerning the existence of equilibrium points of potentials of infinite discrete positive mass distributions appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Equilibrium Points of Logarithmic and Newtonian Potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Clunie, Eremenko, Rossi, J. London Math. Soc. (1993): paper introducing the conjecture about zeros of force fields induced by infinite positive mass distributions.

status_evidence.title: Equilibrium points of logarithmic potentials induced by positive charge distributions. I
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses an operator version of the Clunie–Eremenko–Rossi conjecture; no resolution stated.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains a subject of active investigation, partial results only.

status_evidence.title: Equilibrium points of Newtonian potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up work by Eremenko on the same problem.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing study without complete resolution.
